By revenue, sales, and market capitalization, Walmart is the largest supermarket chain both in the United States and globally [d2][d6][d9]. According to ESM Magazine, Walmart is "the world's largest supermarket chain" with a global turnover of $648.1 billion and over 10,500 stores worldwide [d2], a finding corroborated by GlobalData, which ranks Walmart as "the leading food & grocery retailer in the world (by retail sales)" with revenues of $611,289 million for FY2023 [d9]. By market capitalization, Walmart also ranks first among supermarket chains at $719.59 billion [d4]. However, when measured by number of store locations in the US in 2025, ALDI leads with 2,474 locations across 40 states, followed by Albertsons Companies (2,308 stores) and Publix (1,448 stores) [d5]. Within the US, Kroger is recognized as the largest traditional supermarket company, while Walmart, Kroger, Costco, and Albertsons are considered the "Big 4" US grocery retailers [d6][d1].
